introduce.title: What is Translate PDF Online
introduce.label: Product
introduce.description: Translate PDF Online processes papers, manuals, reports and books through a layout-aware translation workflow. It attempts to place translated text back into the document structure where supported, instead of returning only a plain-text dump.

items.title: Layout-preserving output
items.description: The layout pipeline attempts to reconstruct multi-column text, tables, images and headings. Results vary with the source PDF, fonts, scan quality and page complexity.

items.title: Many language pairs
items.description: Choose a source and target language from the 10 languages currently shown in the selector for academic, technical and professional documents.

items.title: Secure, ephemeral storage
items.description: Files move over HTTPS. Uploaded and generated objects are normally scheduled for deletion after about seven days, subject to the published policy and legal requirements.

items.title: History & task recovery
items.description: The History panel lists every PDF you translate online, so you can reopen a task without re-uploading the same file while it is still retained.

benefits.title: Why teams translate PDFs online with us
benefits.label: Benefits
benefits.description: Review the translated document before download. Complex tables, unusual fonts, handwriting and low-quality scans can still require manual correction.

items.title: Built for dense PDFs
items.description: Tuned for academic and technical layouts — equations, figures and tables — so you can translate dense PDFs online without losing structure where the pipeline supports it.

items.title: Side-by-side preview
items.description: Before you download, compare source and translated pages in the browser with synced scrolling, so you can judge the quality of every PDF you translate online.

items.title: Optional page ranges
items.description: Translate the whole file or only the pages you need. Setting a page range lets you translate a big PDF online faster while saving credits.

usage.title: How to translate a PDF online
usage.description: From upload to download — translate PDF online in five steps:

items.title: Upload
items.description: Drop a PDF or pick a file. Large documents are supported within the limits shown on the translate page, so you can translate a big PDF online in one go.

items.title: Source language
items.description: Select the document language so the engine translates from the correct source when you translate PDF online.

items.title: Target language
items.description: Pick the language you want the PDF translated into — English, Chinese, Spanish, French, Italian, German, Greek, Japanese, Korean or Russian — then start the job.

items.title: Download
items.description: When the job finishes, download the translated PDF from the same screen. The result attempts to preserve the source layout where the pipeline supports it.

items.title: History
items.description: Reopen finished translations from History while the file is still available, so you never lose a PDF you translated online.

features.title: What you get when you translate PDF online
features.description: Practical capabilities for real PDF translation workflows.

items.title: Vector-friendly pipeline
items.description: Uses an advanced AI text-placement path so translated text is placed back into the PDF structure where supported — that is how a PDF translated online keeps its layout.

items.title: Credits & billing
items.description: Pay for what you translate with a credits model tied to pages and product settings, so translating a PDF online stays predictable.

items.title: Account-based processing
items.description: Sign in to process documents, use credits and reopen available jobs from your history across devices.

items.title: Preview before download
items.description: Review source and translated pages in the browser before downloading the result.

items.title: Documentation

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about translating PDF online
faq.description: Quick answers before you translate PDF online. More detail in /docs or email hello@translatepdfonline.com.

items.question: Can I translate both text-based and scanned PDFs?
items.answer: Yes. Text-based PDFs use the layout-aware translation workflow directly. Scanned or image-based PDFs run through OCR first. Blurry scans, handwriting, complex tables, unusual fonts and password-protected files may need preprocessing or manual review.

items.question: Which languages are currently supported?
items.answer: The selector currently supports English, Chinese, Spanish, French, Italian, Greek, Japanese, Korean, German and Russian. Choose a supported source and target language before starting the task.

items.question: Do I need an account, and how is processing charged?
items.answer: Sign-in is required to upload and process documents. Translation and OCR use credits according to the current task settings. The applicable cost and any introductory credits are shown in the product or account interface rather than guaranteed in this page.

items.question: Does all PDF processing happen in my browser?
items.answer: No. You use the browser to upload, review and download files, while OCR, translation and document reconstruction run on backend services. Files are transferred over HTTPS and follow the published retention policy.

items.question: Can I translate only selected pages?
items.answer: Yes. Set a page range when starting the task to process only the pages you need. This can reduce processing time and credit use for longer documents.

items.question: Will the translated PDF preserve its layout?
items.answer: Layout preservation is a goal, not a guarantee. The service attempts to reconstruct text blocks, columns, images and headings where supported. Review the preview because complex tables, unusual fonts, handwriting and low-quality scans can produce differences.
